# test_reverse_words.py
import pytest

from your_module import reverse_words   # adjust the import path/name as needed


# -------------------------
# Happy-path & edge-cases
# -------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "input_str, expected",
    [
        # basic, “normal” sentence
        ("Hello world",               "world Hello"),
        # leading / trailing whitespace and several consecutive spaces
        ("  Hello   world   ",        "world Hello"),
        # mixture of tabs, new-lines, spaces
        ("Hello\tworld\nPython",      "Python world Hello"),
        # single word
        ("Hello",                     "Hello"),
        # empty string
        ("",                          ""),
        # whitespace-only string
        ("   \t   ",                  ""),
        # Unicode / non-ASCII characters
        ("Привет мир",                "мир Привет"),
    ],
)
def test_reverse_words_basic_and_edge_cases(input_str, expected):
    assert reverse_words(input_str) == expected


def test_reverse_words_long_input():
    """A very long string shouldn’t blow up or corrupt the order."""
    words = [f"w{i}" for i in range(1000)]
    original = " ".join(words)
    expected = " ".join(reversed(words))
    assert reverse_words(original) == expected


# --------------
# Error cases
# --------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_input", [None, 123, 12.3, ["a", "b"]])
def test_reverse_words_invalid_input_raises_attribute_error(bad_input):
    """Non-string inputs don’t have `.split()` → AttributeError expected."""
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
        reverse_words(bad_input)
